A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TOAST and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices. The retained material can be matched across the expanded structure in v7.

before.justification: v6 reports original representation analyses, classification accuracy, computational efficiency, translator ablations and zero-shot evaluation, including appendix results.

after.justification: v7 retains original empirical results and adds block-selection evaluations, sensitivity analyses, full-network finetuning, segmentation and text-classification experiments.

M1.justification: v7 adds a block-selection component using normalized linear approximation error and automatic top-k candidate ranking, optionally constrained by a skip budget (Section 3; Algorithms 1–2). v6 used CKA to identify redundancy and deferred automatic selection to future work. The underlying identity and closed-form linear translators remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v7 adds semantic segmentation on SceneParse150 and text classification on AG News using ModernBERT-B (Section 4.3). These extend the task and modality coverage beyond v6's image classification experiments. Zero-shot OpenCLIP evaluation was already present in v6.

E2.justification: Table 11 adds an evaluated comparison of linear-error block selection against cosine distance, CKA, MSE and Euclidean distance. The existing Identity, Linear, MLP and Res-MLP translator comparison is retained; extending these translators to new tasks does not itself change comparator membership.

E3.justification: The similarity analysis changes from token-averaged CKA on 100 samples to linear error using 50 samples and the [CLS] token; translator fitting still generally uses 500 samples. New protocols include Precision@5/Recall@5 evaluation, 20-epoch full-network finetuning and 10-epoch segmentation-head training. The sensitivity study also adds DeiT-B and broader frozen-head testing.

E4.justification: v7 adds block-selection metric and skip-budget analyses (Tables 10–12), extends single-block testing into a systematic six-model sensitivity study, and investigates recovery through end-to-end finetuning (Tables 5 and 19). Existing sample-size, translator-complexity, efficiency and misclassification analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Three-seed averaging and reporting averages with ± values are retained and extended to new experiments. Neither PDF establishes an increase in repeat counts or introduces a new uncertainty-estimation procedure, confidence interval or significance test.

E6.justification: v7 adds quantitative selection, sensitivity, finetuning, segmentation and text-classification results. It also corrects existing entries: Table 4's ImageNet-1k linear accuracy for ViT-L 17→23 changes from 86.20±0.11 to 66.87±0.52, now matching Table 2. Original-head result entries and appendix parameter counts are also revised; most retained classification accuracies and zero-shot results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 2 introduce a formal normalized least-squares residual definition for block similarity, replacing the previous explicit CKA definition. The translator-fitting objective remains unchanged, and no new theorem, proof or theoretical guarantee is supplied.

C1.justification: The introduction adds a claimed contribution of stable, inexpensive automatic block selection and explicitly claims preliminary applicability to segmentation and text classification. These expand the contribution scope beyond v6, although the abstract and conclusion largely retain the original training-free compression claims.

C2.justification: v7 adds interpretations of architecture-dependent sensitivity, model-size effects and finetuning recovery. Section 5 newly discusses limited linear-probe expressivity, missing theoretical characterization and imperfect selection heuristics. Appendix A.2.2 identifies a DeiT-B dataset-dependent reversal, although some new general statements overstate invariance across datasets.

D1.justification: v7 supplies block-selection pseudocode, ModernBERT checkpoint information, new task-training budgets and model-specific finetuning learning rates. It also explicitly specifies 500 approximation samples for the original-head evaluation, previously unstated there. Code access instructions change from a supplementary ZIP to a GitHub link; availability outside the PDFs was not checked.

R1.justification: v7 adds Sun et al. (2023) to the pruning discussion and references supporting ModernBERT, AG News and SceneParse150. The existing related-work organization and positioning around training-free exploitation of intra-network redundancy remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v7 makes copyedits, standardizes model and dataset naming, revises contribution and limitations paragraphs, and reorganizes appendix implementation and classification sections. The main six-section narrative and much existing prose remain intact; the scientific additions do not constitute wholesale rewriting.

P2.justification: v7 adopts a journal layout with different typography, author placement and figure sizing. It redraws Figures 2 and 6 for linear error, combines the former Figures 3 and 4 into subpanels, adds sensitivity plots and numerous experimental tables, and restructures the original-head comparison. Many appendix visualizations are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: v7 addresses v6's unresolved block-selection step with an explicit, evaluated heuristic, tests finetuning recovery and applicability beyond image classification, and corrects misleading entries in Table 4. Expanded limitations better qualify the method's scope. The new sensitivity discussion sometimes overstates dataset invariance despite the documented DeiT-B exception, but this weakness does not outweigh the substantial gains in practical guidance, empirical support and reporting accuracy.
